questions.stem: The two agents in this diagram act on the enzyme that degrades cyclic AMP within the platelet. What is the downstream consequence of their action that reduces platelet activation?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Intracellular cAMP falls, releasing more thromboxane A2

choices.label: D
choices.text: Thromboxane A2 receptors are directly blocked

choices.label: E
choices.text: Intracellular cAMP rises, suppressing platelet activation and aggregation

explanation.summary: Cilostazol and dipyridamole inhibit phosphodiesterase-3, preventing breakdown of cAMP to 5'AMP. Elevated cAMP inhibits platelet activation and aggregation (and causes vasodilation).
explanation.whyCorrect: Cilostazol and dipyridamole inhibit phosphodiesterase-3, preventing breakdown of cAMP to 5'AMP. Elevated cAMP inhibits platelet activation and aggregation (and causes vasodilation).

questions.stem: This pathway shows how a common antiplatelet drug acts on the cyclooxygenase step of arachidonic acid metabolism. What feature of this drug's enzyme inhibition explains why its antiplatelet effect lasts the entire platelet lifespan?

choices.label: A
choices.text: It irreversibly acetylates cyclooxygenase, and platelets cannot synthesize new enzyme

choices.label: B
choices.text: It reversibly competes with arachidonic acid at the active site

choices.label: C
choices.text: It chelates calcium needed for enzyme activity

choices.label: D
choices.text: It antagonizes the thromboxane receptor on platelets

choices.label: E
choices.text: It blocks phospholipase A2, halting substrate supply

explanation.summary: Aspirin irreversibly acetylates COX-1, permanently abolishing thromboxane A2 production. Because anucleate platelets cannot make new enzyme, the effect persists for the ~7-10 day platelet lifespan.
explanation.whyCorrect: Aspirin irreversibly acetylates COX-1, permanently abolishing thromboxane A2 production. Because anucleate platelets cannot make new enzyme, the effect persists for the ~7-10 day platelet lifespan.
